en: (ŚsP II-2 1) The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines, II-2:
Then the Venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the Venerable Subhūti:
How, venerable Subhūti, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, examine these phenomena? Who, venerable Subhūti, is a bodhisattva?
What is the perfection of wisdom?
What is investigation?
When this was said, the venerable Subhūti spoke thus to the venerable Śāradvatīputra:
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, as for what you have said..."
What is a bodhisattva?
It is because awakening itself is his being that he is called a "bodhisattva.
And by means of that awakening, he knows the aspects of all phenomena, yet he does not adhere to those phenomena. Of which phenomena does he know the aspects?
He knows the aspects of form and does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of feeling and does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of perception and does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) and yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of consciousness (*vijñāna*) and yet does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of the eye (*cakṣus*) and yet does not adhere to them.
He knows the characteristics of the ear and does not become attached to them;
he knows the characteristics of the nose and does not become attached to them;
he knows the characteristics of the tongue and does not become attached to them.
He knows the forms of the body but does not adhere to them;
he knows the forms of the mind but does not adhere to them.
He knows the forms of form but does not adhere to them.
He knows the forms of sound and yet does not become attached to them; he knows the forms of smell and yet does not become attached to them;
he knows the forms of taste and yet does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of contact and does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of phenomena and does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of eye-consciousness and does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of auditory consciousness and does not become attached to them; he knows the aspects of olfactory consciousness and does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of gustatory consciousness and does not become attached to them.
He knows the modes of bodily consciousness and does not become attached to them;
he knows the modes of mental consciousness and does not become attached to them.
He knows the modes of visual contact and does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of auditory contact, yet he does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of olfactory contact, yet he does not adhere to them.
He knows the modes of tongue-contact and does not become attached to them; he knows the modes of body-contact and does not become attached to them;
he knows the modes of mind-contact and does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of feeling conditioned by eye-contact, yet he does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of feeling conditioned by ear-contact, yet he does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of feeling conditioned by nose-contact, yet he does not adhere to them.
He knows the modes of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the modes of feeling conditioned by body-contact, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the modes of feeling conditioned by mind-contact, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the characteristics of the earth element, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the characteristics of the water element, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the characteristics of the fire element, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the characteristics of the wind element, yet he does not adhere to them; he knows the characteristics of the space element, yet he does not adhere to them;
he knows the characteristics of the consciousness element, yet he does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of ignorance, yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of formative forces, yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of consciousness, yet does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of name-and-form, yet he does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of the six sense bases, yet he does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of contact, yet he does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of sensation, yet does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of craving, yet does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of grasping, yet does not become attached to them.

He knows the aspects of existence, yet he does not adhere to them; he knows the aspects of birth, yet he does not adhere to them; he knows the aspects of old age and death, yet he does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of the perfection of generosity, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the aspects of the perfection of ethical discipline, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the perfection of patience, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of the perfection of vigor, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the perfection of meditative concentration, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the perfection of wisdom, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of internal emptiness and yet does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of external emptiness and yet does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of internal-and-external emptiness and yet does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of the emptiness of emptiness, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the aspects of great emptiness, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the emptiness of the ultimate truth, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of conditioned emptiness and yet does not adhere to them; he knows the aspects of unconditioned emptiness and yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the aspects of absolute emptiness and yet does not [adhere to them].
He does not become attached therein;
he knows the aspects of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, yet he does not become attached therein;
he knows the aspects of the emptiness of non-dispersal, yet he does not become attached therein.
He knows the aspects of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the emptiness of all phenomena, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the emptiness of specific characteristics, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of the emptiness of non-apprehension, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the aspects of the emptiness of non-existence, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of the applications of mindfulness, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the right efforts, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the modes of the bases of psychic power and does not adhere to them; he knows the modes of the faculties and does not adhere to them;
he knows the modes of the powers and does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of the factors of enlightenment, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the noble eightfold path, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the noble truths, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the modes of the meditative concentrations and yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the modes of the immeasurables and yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the modes of the formless attainments and yet does not adhere to them.
He knows the aspects of the liberations, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the successive meditative attainments, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the modes of the superknowledges and yet does not adhere to them;
he knows the modes of the meditative concentrations and yet does not adhere to them; he knows the modes of the gateways of the dhāraṇīs and yet does not adhere to them.

He knows the modes of the powers of a Tathāgata, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the modes of the grounds of self-confidence, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the modes of the analytical knowledges, yet he does not become attached to them.
He knows the aspects of great loving-kindness, yet he does not become attached to them; he knows the aspects of great compassion, yet he does not become attached to them;
he knows the aspects of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, yet he does not become attached to them.
He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what are the aspects of all dharmas?
Subhūti replied:
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, those aspects, those marks, and those signs by which all dharmas are characterized."

That is to say, by whatever forms, sounds, odors, tastes, or tangibles, or by internal or external phenomena— whether conditioned or unconditioned— by which [phenomena] are characterized through their respective aspects, marks, and signs;
these are called the aspects of all phenomena.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, as to what you have asked: "What is the perfection of wisdom?"
This, venerable Śāradvatīputra, which is called the perfection of wisdom, is a state of cessation. Why is it a state of cessation?
It is called a state of cessation, venerable Śāradvatīputra, because it has ceased from the aggregates; it is called a state of cessation because it has desisted from the elements.
It is called "having come to rest" because one has desisted from the sense-bases; it is called "having come to rest" because one has desisted from all afflictions;
it is called "having come to rest" because one has desisted from all courses of views.
Having desisted, having ceased from the six states of existence—that is what it is called.
Having desisted, having ceased from the perfection of generosity—that is what it is called; having desisted, having ceased from the perfection of ethical discipline—that is what it is called.
That which has reached its limit, that which has ceased, regarding the perfection of patience—that is called "having reached its limit, having ceased.
That which has reached its limit, that which has ceased, regarding the perfection of vigor—that is called "having reached its limit, having ceased.
That which has reached its limit, that which has ceased, regarding the perfection of meditative concentration—that is called "having reached its limit, having ceased."
Having desisted, having ceased from the perfection of wisdom—that is what it is called. Having desisted, having ceased from internal emptiness—that is what it is called.
Having desisted, having ceased from external emptiness—that is what it is called.

The cessation of attachment due to the cessation of internal and external emptiness is called "cessation of attachment"; the cessation of attachment due to the cessation of the emptiness of emptiness is called "cessation of attachment"; the cessation of attachment due to the cessation of great emptiness is called "cessation of attachment."
That which has ceased, having desisted from ultimate emptiness—that is called "ceased. That which has ceased, having desisted from conditioned emptiness—that is called "ceased.
That which has ceased, having desisted from unconditioned emptiness—that is called "ceased."

It is called "restraint" because one has desisted from ultimate emptiness; it is called "restraint" because one has desisted from the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end; it is called "restraint" because one has desisted from the emptiness of non-dispersal.
That which is the cessation, the desisting, from the emptiness of intrinsic nature—that is called "having ceased.
That which is the cessation, the desisting, from the emptiness of all phenomena—that is called "having ceased.
That which is the cessation, the desisting, from the emptiness of specific characteristics—that is called "having ceased."
That which is the cessation of craving is called the emptiness of the non-apprehensibility of craving; that which is the cessation of craving is called the emptiness of the non-existence of craving;
that which is the cessation of craving is called the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of craving.
It is called "having desisted" because it has the nature of being empty of the state of having desisted.
It is called "having desisted" because it has desisted from the applications of mindfulness;
it is called "having desisted" because it has desisted from the right efforts.
Having desisted, having ceased from the bases of psychic power—that is what is called [desisting]; having desisted, having ceased from the faculties—that is what is called [desisting];
having desisted, having ceased from the powers—that is what is called [desisting].
It is called "having desisted" because one has desisted from the factors of enlightenment; it is called "having desisted" because one has desisted from the noble eightfold path;
it is called "having desisted" because one has desisted from the noble truths.

Having desisted from the meditative absorptions (dhyāna), that is called "desisted"; having desisted from the immeasurables (apramāṇa), that is called "desisted"; having desisted from the formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), that is called "desisted."
Having desisted, having ceased from the liberations—that is what is meant; having desisted, having ceased from the successive attainments of meditative dwelling—that is what is meant;
having desisted, having ceased from the gateways to liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—that is what is meant.

That which has desisted from the superknowledges is called "desisted"; that which has desisted from the meditative absorptions is called "desisted"; that which has desisted from the gateways of the dhāraṇīs is called "desisted."

He has desisted from the powers of a Tathāgata; therefore it is said that he has desisted. He has desisted from the grounds of self-confidence; therefore it is said that he has desisted. He has desisted from the analytical knowledges; therefore it is said that he has desisted.
That which is the cessation, the desisting, from great loving-kindness is called "having ceased"; that which is the cessation, the desisting, from great compassion is called "having ceased";
that which is the cessation, the desisting, from the unique qualities of a Buddha is called "having ceased."

That which has reached its limit and ceased with respect to omniscience is called "having reached the limit"; that which has reached its limit and ceased with respect to the knowledge of the aspects of the path is called "having reached the limit";
that which has reached its limit and ceased with respect to the knowledge of all aspects is called "having reached the limit."
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this is a perfection, namely, the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore,
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, as to what you asked, "What is the investigation?"— it is this very thing.
In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not examine form as permanent, nor as impermanent;
he does not examine form as pleasant, nor as painful;
he does not examine form as self, nor as non-self.

Subhūti said:
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is empty of form. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is empty of form is neither form nor arising."
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of form is not form;
feeling, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of feeling, and that which, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty is not feeling, nor is it arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of feeling is not feeling.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, perception is empty of perception; Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is empty of perception is neither perception nor its arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of perception is not perception.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, volitional formations are empty of volitional formations; Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is empty of volitional formations is neither those volitional formations nor their arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of formations is not those formations.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, consciousness is empty of consciousness; that which, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty is not consciousness, nor is it arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of consciousness is not that consciousness.
The eye, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the eye; that which, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty is neither the eye nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the eye is not the eye.
The ear, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the ear; that which, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty is neither the ear nor its arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the ear is not the ear;
the nose, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of a nose; and that which, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty is not the nose, nor is it arising.
In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the nose is not the nose;
the tongue, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of a tongue; and that which is empty of a tongue, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither the tongue nor its arising.
In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the tongue is not the tongue.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the body is empty of the body; that which is empty, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither the body nor its arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the body is not the body.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the mind is empty of the mind; that which is empty, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither the mind nor its arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the mind is not the mind.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is empty of form; that which, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty is not form, nor is it arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of form is not form.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, sound is empty of sound;
and that which is empty is neither sound nor an arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of sound is not sound.
O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, smell is empty of smell; that which is empty is not smell, nor is it an arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of smell is not smell.
Taste, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of taste; that which is empty is not taste, nor is it an arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of taste is not taste;
touch, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of touch,
and that which is empty is neither touch nor arising.
In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of contact is not contact;
venerable Śāradvatīputra, phenomena are empty of phenomena, and that which is empty is neither a phenomenon nor an arising.
In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of phenomena is not those phenomena.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness.
That which is empty is neither eye-consciousness nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of eye-consciousness is not eye-consciousness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, auditory consciousness is empty of auditory consciousness;
and that which is empty is neither auditory consciousness nor its arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of auditory consciousness is not auditory consciousness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, olfactory consciousness is empty of olfactory consciousness;
and that which is empty is neither olfactory consciousness nor its arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of olfactory consciousness is not olfactory consciousness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, tongue-consciousness is empty of tongue-consciousness;
and that which is empty is neither tongue-consciousness nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of tongue-consciousness is not that tongue-consciousness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, body-consciousness is empty of body-consciousness;

and that which is empty is not that body-consciousness, nor is it arising. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, mental consciousness is empty of mental consciousness;
and that which is empty is neither mental consciousness nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of mental consciousness is not mental consciousness.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, eye-contact is empty of eye-contact; that which is empty is neither eye-contact nor its arising. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of eye-contact is not eye-contact. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, ear-contact is empty of ear-contact.
And that which is empty is neither ear-contact nor arising.
In this manner, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of ear-contact is not ear-contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, nose-contact is empty of nose-contact.
And that which is empty is neither nose-contact nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of nose-contact is not nose-contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, tongue-contact is empty of tongue-contact.
And that which is empty is neither tongue-contact nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, body-contact is empty of body-contact.
And that which is empty is neither body-contact nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of body-contact is not body-contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, mind-contact is empty of mind-contact.
And that which is empty is neither mental contact nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of mental contact is not mental contact.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling conditioned by visual contact is empty of feeling conditioned by visual contact.
That which is empty is neither the feeling conditioned by eye-contact nor its arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by ear-contact.

And that which is empty is neither the sensation conditioned by auditory contact nor its arising; in this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the sensation conditioned by auditory contact is not that sensation conditioned by auditory contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact;
and that which is empty is neither the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is not the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;
and that which is empty is neither the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by bodily contact;
and that which is empty is neither the feeling conditioned by bodily contact nor its arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is not the feeling conditioned by bodily contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling conditioned by mental contact is empty of feeling conditioned by mental contact;
and that which is empty is neither feeling conditioned by mental contact nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not that feeling conditioned by mental contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the earth element is empty of the earth element;
and that which is empty is neither the earth element nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the earth element is not the earth element.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the water element is empty of the water element;
that which is empty is neither the water element nor its arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the water element is not the water element.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the fire element is empty of the fire element;
and that which is empty is neither the fire element nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the fire element is not the fire element.
The wind element, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the wind element;
and that which is empty is not the wind element, nor is it an arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the wind element is not the wind element.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the space-element is empty of the space-element;
and that which is empty is neither the space-element nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the space-element is not the space-element.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the consciousness element is empty of the consciousness element;
and that which is empty is not the consciousness element, nor is it an arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the consciousness element is not the consciousness element.
(ŚsP II-2 34) Venerable Śāradvatīputra, ignorance is empty of ignorance;
and that which is empty is neither ignorance nor its arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of ignorance is not ignorance;
the formative forces, venerable Śāradvatīputra, are empty of formative forces,
and that which is empty is neither those formative forces nor their arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of formations is not those formations. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, consciousness is empty of consciousness;
and that which is empty is not consciousness, nor is it arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of consciousness is not that consciousness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, name-and-form is empty of name-and-form;
and that which is empty is neither name-and-form nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of name-and-form is not name-and-form.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the six sense bases are empty of the six sense bases;
and that which is empty is neither the six sense bases nor their arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the six sense bases is not the six sense bases.
Contact, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of contact;
and that which is empty is neither contact nor an arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of contact is not contact.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling is empty of feeling;
and that which is empty is neither feeling nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of feeling is not feeling.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, craving is empty of craving;
and that which is empty is neither craving nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method of exposition, that which is the non-arising of craving is not craving.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, grasping is empty of grasping;
and that which is empty is neither grasping nor arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of grasping is not grasping.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, existence is empty of existence; and that which is empty is neither existence nor arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of existence is not existence.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, birth is empty of birth;
and that which is empty is neither birth nor arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of birth is not birth.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, old age and death are empty of old age and death;
and that which is empty is neither old age and death nor arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of old age and death is not old age and death.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of generosity is empty of the perfection of generosity;
and that which is empty is neither the perfection of generosity nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline;
and that which is empty is neither the perfection of ethical discipline nor its production.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the perfection of ethical discipline—
Non-arising, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is not that perfection of ethical discipline; the perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience,
and that which is empty is neither the perfection of patience nor arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience;
venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor,
and that which is empty is neither the perfection of vigor nor its arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor;
the perfection of meditation, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the perfection of meditation,
and that which is empty is neither the perfection of meditation nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation;
venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom,
and that which is empty is neither the perfection of wisdom nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, internal emptiness is empty by virtue of internal emptiness;
and that which is empty is neither internal emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness itself;
and as for external emptiness, venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is empty by virtue of being external emptiness—
that which is empty is neither external emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of external emptiness is not that external emptiness;
for, venerable Śāradvatīputra, internal-external emptiness is empty of internal-external emptiness,
and that which is empty is neither internal-external emptiness nor arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of internal-and-external emptiness is not internal-and-external emptiness itself.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of emptiness is empty by virtue of the emptiness of emptiness;
and that which is empty is neither the emptiness of emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of emptiness is not that emptiness of emptiness;
the great emptiness, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the great emptiness,
and that which is empty is neither the great emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of great emptiness is not that great emptiness;
the emptiness of the ultimate, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the emptiness of the ultimate,
and that which is empty is neither the emptiness of the ultimate nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of ultimate emptiness is not itself ultimate emptiness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, conditioned emptiness is empty of conditioned emptiness;
and that which is empty is neither conditioned emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of conditioned emptiness is not itself conditioned emptiness;
for, venerable Śāradvatīputra, absolute emptiness is empty by virtue of absolute emptiness.
That which is empty is neither absolute emptiness nor arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of absolute emptiness is not itself absolute emptiness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, beginningless-and-endless emptiness is empty by virtue of being beginningless-and-endless emptiness.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end nor is it arising.

By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is not itself the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of non-dispersal is empty by virtue of the emptiness of non-dispersal.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of non-dispersal nor is it arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-dispersal is not the emptiness of non-dispersal.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, intrinsic nature is empty by means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
That which is empty is neither intrinsic emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of intrinsic emptiness is not intrinsic emptiness itself.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of all phenomena is empty by means of the emptiness of all phenomena.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of all phenomena nor is it arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena is not itself the emptiness of all phenomena.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is empty by means of the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of its own characteristic nor is it arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of its own characteristic is not itself the emptiness of its own characteristic.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty by virtue of the emptiness of the non-apprehension of emptiness.
That which is empty is neither non-apprehension-emptiness nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of non-apprehension-emptiness is not non-apprehension-emptiness;
for, venerable Śāradvatīputra, emptiness of non-existence is empty by way of the emptiness of non-existence.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of non-existence nor is it arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence is not the emptiness of non-existence.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty by means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of intrinsic nature nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty by virtue of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
That which is empty is neither the emptiness of non-existence by way of intrinsic nature nor is it arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence by way of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of non-existence by way of intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the applications of mindfulness are empty; those applications of mindfulness which are empty are neither the applications of mindfulness nor are they arising.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness;
venerable Śāradvatīputra, the right efforts are empty of right efforts,
and that which is empty of right efforts is neither those right efforts nor their arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the right efforts is not those right efforts;
the bases of psychic power, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, are empty of the bases of psychic power, and that which is empty is neither those bases of psychic power nor their arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the faculties are empty of faculties; and that which is empty is neither those faculties nor their arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the faculties is not those faculties.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the powers are empty of powers; and that which is empty is neither those powers nor their arising."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the powers is not those powers;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment, and that which is empty is not those factors of enlightenment, nor is it arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the factors of enlightenment is not those factors of enlightenment.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the noble eightfold path is empty of the noble eightfold path; and that which is empty is neither the path nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of the noble eightfold path is not the path.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the noble truths are empty of the noble truths.
And those things which are empty are not the noble truths, nor is there arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the noble truths is not those noble truths.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the meditative absorptions are empty of meditative absorptions.
And those which are empty are neither meditations nor an arising; by this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the meditations is not those meditations.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the immeasurables are empty of immeasurables.
And those which are empty are neither the immeasurables nor production.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-production of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the formless attainments are empty of formless attainments.
And those which are empty are not the formless attainments, nor are they arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the liberations are empty of liberations.
And those which are empty are not the liberations, nor are they arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the liberations is not those liberations.
The successive attainments of meditative dwelling, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, are empty of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling.
And those which are empty are not the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, nor are they non-arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling is not those successive attainments of meditative dwelling.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are [not] by way of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
And those things which are empty are not the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—nor are they arising.
In this manner, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those doors of liberation themselves.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the superknowledges are empty; [they are empty] by means of the superknowledges.
And those which are empty are not the superknowledges, nor are they arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges;
the concentrations, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, are empty of concentrations.

And those which are empty are not those concentrations, nor is there arising. By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of concentrations is not those concentrations. O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the gateways of dhāraṇī are empty of the gateways of dhāraṇī;
and those which are empty are not those gateways of dhāraṇī, nor is there arising.
In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the gateways of dhāraṇī is not those gateways of dhāraṇī;
likewise, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the powers of a Tathāgata,
and that which is empty is neither those powers of a Tathāgata nor arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the powers of a Tathāgata is not those powers of a Tathāgata;
the grounds of self-confidence, venerable Śāradvatīputra, are empty of the grounds of self-confidence, and that which is empty is neither those grounds of self-confidence nor arising.

By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence; Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the analytical knowledges are empty of analytical knowledges, and that which is empty is neither those analytical knowledges nor their arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the analytical knowledges is not those analytical knowledges.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, great loving-kindness is empty of great loving-kindness;
and that which is empty is neither great loving-kindness nor its arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is the non-arising of great loving-kindness is not [itself] great loving-kindness.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, great compassion is empty of great compassion;
and that which is empty is neither great compassion nor its arising. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of great compassion is not great compassion.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha.

And those which are empty are not the unique qualities of a Buddha, nor are they an arising. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the unique qualities of a Buddha is not those unique qualities of a Buddha.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, omniscience is empty of omniscience;
and that which is empty is not omniscience, nor is it an arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of omniscience is not omniscience;

venerable Śāradvatīputra, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is empty of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and that which is empty is neither the knowledge of the aspects of the path nor its arising. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path—
That knowledge of the aspects of the path,
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of the knowledge of all aspects;
and that which is empty is not the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it an arising.
"In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-arising of omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) is not that omniscience.
He asked: "For what reason, venerable Subhūti, do you speak thus? [Subhūti replied: "That which is the passing away of form is not that form."

That which is the passing away of feeling is not that feeling; that which is the passing away of perception is not that perception; that which is the passing away of volitional formations is not those volitional formations.
That which is the passing away of consciousness is not that consciousness;
that which is the passing away of the eye is not that eye;
that which is the passing away of the ear is not that ear.
That which is the exhaustion of the nose is not the nose; that which is the exhaustion of the tongue is not the tongue;
that which is the exhaustion of the body is not the body.
That which is the passing away of the mind is not that mind;
that which is the passing away of form is not that form;
that which is the passing away of sound is not that sound.
That which is the cessation of odor is not odor;
that which is the cessation of taste is not taste;
that which is the cessation of touch is not touch.
That which is the cessation of phenomena is not those phenomena;
that which is the cessation of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness,
and that which is the cessation of ear-consciousness is not that ear-consciousness.
That which is the cessation of olfactory consciousness is not that olfactory consciousness;
that which is the cessation of gustatory consciousness is not that gustatory consciousness;
that which is the cessation of tactile consciousness is not that tactile consciousness.
That which is the cessation of mental consciousness is not that mental consciousness;
that which is the cessation of visual contact is not that visual contact;
that which is the cessation of auditory contact is not that auditory contact.
That which is the cessation of olfactory contact is not olfactory contact;
that which is the cessation of gustatory contact is not gustatory contact;
that which is the cessation of tactile contact is not tactile contact.
That which is the cessation of mental contact is not that mental contact.
That which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by visual contact is not that feeling conditioned by visual contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by auditory contact is not that feeling conditioned by auditory contact.
That which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by nose-contact is not that feeling conditioned by nose-contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by body-contact is not that feeling conditioned by body-contact.
That which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not that feeling conditioned by mental contact.
That which is the cessation of the earth element is not that earth element;
that which is the cessation of the water element is not that water element.
That which is the cessation of the fire element is not the fire element;
that which is the cessation of the air element is not the air element;
that which is the cessation of the space element is not the space element.
That which is the cessation of the element of consciousness is not that element of consciousness.
That which is the cessation of ignorance is not that ignorance.
That which is the cessation of formative forces is not those formative forces;
that which is the cessation of consciousness is not that consciousness;
that which is the cessation of name-and-form is not that name-and-form.
That which is the cessation of the six sense bases is not the six sense bases; that which is the cessation of contact is not contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling is not feeling.
That which is the exhaustion of craving is not that craving; that which is the exhaustion of clinging is not that clinging;
that which is the exhaustion of existence is not that existence.
That which is the cessation of birth is not that birth;
that which is the cessation of aging and death is not that aging and death.
That which is the cessation of the perfection of generosity is not that perfection of generosity.
That which is the exhaustion of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline;
that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience;
that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor.
That which is the exhaustion of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation;
that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom. That which is the exhaustion of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness.
That which is the cessation of external emptiness is not external emptiness;
that which is the cessation of internal-external emptiness is not internal-external emptiness;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of emptiness is not the emptiness of emptiness.
That which is the cessation of great emptiness is not that great emptiness;
that which is the cessation of ultimate emptiness is not that ultimate emptiness;
that which is the cessation of conditioned emptiness is not that conditioned emptiness.
That which is the passing away of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not the emptiness of the unconditioned;
that which is the passing away of absolute emptiness is not absolute emptiness;
that which is the passing away of the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end is not the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end.

That which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-dispersal is not that emptiness of non-dispersal; that which is the cessation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not that emptiness of intrinsic nature;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of all phenomena is not that emptiness of all phenomena.
That which is the cessation of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not that emptiness of specific characteristics;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-apprehension is not that emptiness of non-apprehension;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-existence is not that emptiness of non-existence.
That which is the passing away of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not that emptiness of intrinsic nature;
that which is the passing away of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not that emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
That which is the passing away of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness.

That which is the exhaustion of the right efforts is not those right efforts; that which is the exhaustion of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power; that which is the exhaustion of the faculties is not those faculties.
That which is the exhaustion of the powers is not those powers; that which is the exhaustion of the factors of awakening is not those factors of awakening;
that which is the exhaustion of the noble eightfold path is not that noble eightfold path.

That which is the passing away of the noble truths is not those noble truths; that which is the passing away of the meditative absorptions is not those meditative absorptions; that which is the passing away of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables.
That which is the cessation of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments;
that which is the cessation of the liberations is not those liberations; that which is the cessation of the successive meditative attainments...
The cessation of those successive meditative attainments is not those successive meditative attainments;
the cessation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those gateways to liberation;
the cessation of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges.

That which is the exhaustion of the meditative concentrations is not those meditative concentrations; that which is the exhaustion of the gateways of mnemonic formulas is not those gateways of mnemonic formulas; that which is the exhaustion of the powers of a Tathāgata is not those powers of a Tathāgata.
That which is the exhaustion of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence;
that which is the exhaustion of the analytical knowledges is not those analytical knowledges; that which is the exhaustion of great loving-kindness is not that great loving-kindness.
That which is the cessation of great compassion is not great compassion;
that which is the cessation of the unique qualities of a Buddha is not the unique qualities of a Buddha;
that which is the cessation of omniscience is not omniscience.

That which is the cessation of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not the knowledge of the aspects of the path; that which is the cessation of the knowledge of all aspects is not the knowledge of all aspects.
Subhūti said:

For in this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is cessation, that which is form, and that which is non-duality—all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics. That which is cessation, that which is feeling, and that which is non-duality;
and that which is cessation, that which is perception, and that which is non-duality—[all these are likewise].

That which is cessation and those which are the formative forces, and that which is non-duality; and that which is cessation and that which is consciousness, and that which is non-duality— all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
That which is exhaustion and that which is the eye, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and that which is the ear, and that which is non-duality;
that which is exhaustion and that which is the nose, and that which is non-duality.
That which is the tongue and that non-duality, that which is the body and that non-duality,
and that which is the mind and that non-duality; and that which is the exhaustion [of phenomena]— [all these are equal].

All these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics. That which is cessation and that which is form are non-dual; that which is cessation and that which is sound are non-dual.

That which is decay and that which is odor, and that which is non-duality; that which is decay and that which is taste, and that which is non-duality; that which is decay and that which is tangibility, and that which is non-duality.
That which is cessation, those which are phenomena, and that which is non-duality—

all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
That which is cessation and that which is eye-consciousness, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is ear-consciousness, and that which is non-duality;
that which is cessation and that which is nose-consciousness, and that which is non-duality.
That which is cessation and that which is tongue-consciousness, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is body-consciousness, and that which is non-duality;
and that which is cessation and that which is mind-consciousness, and that which is non-duality.
All these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being characterless.
That which is cessation and that which is eye-contact and that which is non-duality, and that which is cessation and that which is ear-contact and that which is non-duality—[all these are likewise].
That which is cessation and that which is olfactory contact, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is gustatory contact, and that which is non-duality;
that which is cessation and that which is tactile contact, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation, that which is mental contact, and that which is non-duality—all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
That which is cessation, that which is the feeling conditioned by visual contact, and that which is non-duality—[all these are likewise].

That which is exhaustion and that which is the feeling conditioned by auditory contact, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and that which is the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact, and that which is non-duality;
that which is exhaustion and that which is the feeling conditioned by gustatory contact, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation, that which is the feeling conditioned by body-contact, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation, that which is the feeling conditioned by mind-contact, and that which is non-duality—all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.

That which is disintegration and that which is the earth element, and that which is non-duality; that which is disintegration and that which is the water element, and that which is non-duality; that which is disintegration and that which is the fire element, and that which is non-duality.
That which is disintegration and that which is the wind element, and their non-duality; that which is disintegration and that which is the space element, and their non-duality;
and that which is disintegration and that which is the consciousness element, and their non-duality.

All these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.

That which is cessation and that which is ignorance, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and those which are the formative forces, and that which is non-duality—[all these are likewise].
That which is cessation and that which is consciousness, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is name-and-form, and that which is non-duality;
that which is cessation and that which is the six sense-bases, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation and that which is contact, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is sensation, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is craving, and that which is non-duality.
That which is cessation and that which is appropriation,
and that which is non-duality;
and that which is cessation and that which is existence, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation, that which is birth, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation, that which is aging and death, and that which is non-duality—all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.

That which is exhaustion and that which is the perfection of generosity, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and that which is the perfection of ethical discipline, and that which is non-duality;
that which is exhaustion and that which is the perfection of patience, and that which is non-duality.
That which is exhaustion, that which is the perfection of vigor, and that which is non-duality;
that which is exhaustion, that which is the perfection of meditation, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion, that which is the perfection of wisdom, and that which is non-duality.

All these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics. That which is cessation and that which is internal emptiness are non-dual; that which is cessation and that which is external emptiness are non-dual.
That which is cessation and that which is internal and external emptiness, and their non-duality;
that which is cessation and that which is the emptiness of emptiness, and their non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is great emptiness, and their non-duality.
That which is exhaustion and that which is ultimate emptiness, and their non-duality;
that which is exhaustion and that which is conditioned emptiness, and their non-duality; that which is exhaustion and that which is unconditioned emptiness, and their non-duality.
That which is cessation and that which is absolute emptiness, and that which is non-duality;

that which is cessation and that which is the emptiness of the beginningless and endless, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is the emptiness of non-dispersal, and that which is non-duality.
That which is cessation and that which is emptiness of intrinsic nature, and that which is non-duality;

that which is cessation and that which is emptiness of all phenomena, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is emptiness of specific characteristics, and that which is non-duality.
That which is exhaustion and that which is the emptiness of non-apprehension, and that which is non-duality;

that which is exhaustion and that which is the emptiness of non-existence, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and that which is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation, that which is the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and that which is non-duality—all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being characterless.
That which is cessation and those which are the applications of mindfulness, and that which is non-duality—[all these are likewise].

That which is exhaustion and those which are the right efforts, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and those which are the bases of psychic power, and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and those which are the faculties, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation and those which are the powers and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and those which are the factors of enlightenment and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is the noble eightfold path and that which is non-duality.
That which is cessation and those noble truths, and that which is non-duality;
that which is cessation and those meditative absorptions, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and those immeasurables, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation and those formless attainments, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and those liberations, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and those serial meditative attainments, and that which is non-duality.
That which is exhaustion and those gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and that which is non-duality;
that which is exhaustion and those supernormal powers and that which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and those meditative concentrations and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation, those gateways of dhāraṇī, and that which is non-duality—all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being characterless.
That which is cessation, those powers of a Tathāgata, and that which is non-duality—[all these are likewise].

And that which is exhaustion, and those which are the grounds of self-confidence, and that which is non-duality; and that which is exhaustion, and those which are the analytical knowledges, and that which is non-duality;
and that which is exhaustion, and that which is great loving-kindness, and that which is non-duality.

That which is cessation, that which is great compassion, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation, those which are the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and that which is non-duality— all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
That which is exhaustion and that which is the fruit of stream-entry, which is non-duality; that which is exhaustion and that which is the fruit of once-returning, which is non-duality;
that which is exhaustion and that which is the fruit of non-returning, which is non-duality.
That which is cessation, that which is arhatship, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation, that which is pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and that which is non-duality—
all these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
That which is cessation and that which is omniscience, and that which is non-duality;

that which is cessation and that which is the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and that which is non-duality; that which is cessation and that which is the knowledge of all aspects, and that which is non-duality.

All these phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the cessation of form is not form;
that which is the cessation of feeling is not feeling.
That which is the cessation of perception is not that perception;
that which is the cessation of volitional formations is not those volitional formations; that which is the cessation of consciousness is not that consciousness.
That which is the passing away of the eye is not that eye;
that which is the passing away of the ear is not that ear;
that which is the passing away of the nose is not that nose.
That which is the disintegration of the tongue is not the tongue;
that which is the disintegration of the body is not the body;
that which is the disintegration of the mind is not the mind.
That which is the cessation of form is not that form; that which is the cessation of sound is not that sound; that which is the cessation of odor is not that odor.
That which is the exhaustion of taste is not taste;
that which is the exhaustion of touch is not touch; that which is the exhaustion of phenomena is not those phenomena.
That which is the cessation of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness;
that which is the cessation of ear-consciousness is not that ear-consciousness;
that which is the cessation of nose-consciousness is not that nose-consciousness.
That which is the cessation of tongue-consciousness is not that tongue-consciousness;
that which is the cessation of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness; that which is the cessation of mind-consciousness is not that mind-consciousness.
That which is the cessation of eye-contact is not eye-contact;
that which is the cessation of ear-contact is not ear-contact;
that which is the cessation of nose-contact is not nose-contact.
That which is the cessation of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact;
that which is the cessation of body-contact is not body-contact;
that which is the cessation of mind-contact is not mind-contact.
That which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not that feeling conditioned by ear-contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by nose-contact is not that feeling conditioned by nose-contact.
That which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;

that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by body-contact is not that feeling conditioned by body-contact; that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by mind-contact is not that feeling conditioned by mind-contact.
That which is the cessation of the earth element is not the earth element;
that which is the cessation of the water element is not the water element;
that which is the cessation of the fire element is not the fire element.
That which is the cessation of the wind element is not the wind element;
that which is the cessation of the space element is not the space element;
that which is the cessation of the consciousness element is not the consciousness element.
That which is the cessation of ignorance is not ignorance;
that which is the cessation of volitional formations is not those volitional formations;
that which is the cessation of consciousness is not that consciousness.
That which is the cessation of name-and-form is not name-and-form; that which is the cessation of the six sense-bases is not the six sense-bases;
that which is the cessation of contact is not contact.
That which is the cessation of feeling is not that feeling;
that which is the cessation of craving is not that craving; that which is the cessation of clinging is not that clinging.
That which is the cessation of existence is not existence; that which is the cessation of birth is not birth; that which is the cessation of old age and death is not old age and death.

That which is the exhaustion of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity; that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline;
that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience.
That which is the exhaustion of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor; that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation;
that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom.
That which is the cessation of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness;
that which is the cessation of external emptiness is not external emptiness.
That which is the cessation of internal-external emptiness is not internal-external emptiness;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of emptiness is not the emptiness of emptiness;
that which is the cessation of great emptiness is not great emptiness.
That which is the cessation of the emptiness of the ultimate is not the emptiness of the ultimate;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of the conditioned is not the emptiness of the conditioned;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not the emptiness of the unconditioned.
That which is the cessation of absolute emptiness is not absolute emptiness;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is not the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-dispersal is not the emptiness of non-dispersal.
That which is the cessation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not that emptiness of intrinsic nature;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of all phenomena is not that emptiness of all phenomena;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not that emptiness of specific characteristics.
That which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-apprehension is not the emptiness of non-apprehension;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-existence is not the emptiness of non-existence;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

That which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-existence by its own nature is not that emptiness of non-existence by its own nature; that which is the cessation of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness;
that which is the cessation of the right efforts is not those right efforts.
That which is the passing away of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power; that which is the passing away of the faculties is not those faculties;
that which is the passing away of the powers is not those powers.
That which is the passing away of the factors of enlightenment is not those factors of enlightenment;
that which is the passing away of the noble eightfold path is not that noble eightfold path; that which is the passing away of the noble truths is not those noble truths.

That which is the exhaustion of the meditative absorptions is not those meditative absorptions; that which is the exhaustion of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables; that which is the exhaustion of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments.
That which is the exhaustion of the liberations is not those liberations;

that which is the exhaustion of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling is not those successive attainments of meditative dwelling; that which is the exhaustion of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

That which is the exhaustion of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges; that which is the exhaustion of the meditative concentrations is not those meditative concentrations; that which is the exhaustion of the gateways of mnemonic formulas is not those gateways of mnemonic formulas.

That which is the exhaustion of the powers of a Tathāgata is not those powers of a Tathāgata; that which is the non-arising of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence; that which is the exhaustion of the analytical knowledges is not those analytical knowledges.
That which is the exhaustion of great loving-kindness is not great loving-kindness; that which is the exhaustion of great compassion is not compassion;
that which is the exhaustion of the unique qualities of a buddha is not those unique qualities of a buddha.
That which is the exhaustion of omniscience is not omniscience;

that which is the exhaustion of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not the knowledge of the aspects of the path; that which is the exhaustion of the knowledge of all aspects is not the knowledge of all aspects.
He said: "For what reason, Venerable Subhūti, do you speak thus, that this which is called 'form' is designated as a reckoning of non-duality?"

That which is called "feeling" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "perception" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "formative forces" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called "consciousness" is merely a designation for this non-duality;
that which is called "the eye" is merely a designation for this non-duality;
that which is called "the ear" is merely a designation for this non-duality.
That which is called "nose" is a designation for non-duality; that which is called "tongue" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "body" is a designation for non-duality.
That which is called "mind" is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called "form" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "sound" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called "odor" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "taste" is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called "touch" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called "phenomena" (dharmas) is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called "eye-consciousness" is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called "ear-consciousness" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called "nose-consciousness" is a designation for non-duality; that which is called "tongue-consciousness" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "body-consciousness" is a designation for non-duality.
That which is called "mental consciousness" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "eye-contact" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "ear-contact" is a designation for non-duality.
That which is called "nose-contact" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "tongue-contact" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "body-contact" is a designation for non-duality.
That which is called "mental contact" is a designation made for the non-dual;

that which is called "feeling conditioned by visual contact" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "feeling conditioned by auditory contact" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called "feeling conditioned by nose-contact" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "feeling conditioned by tongue-contact" is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called "feeling conditioned by body-contact" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called "feeling conditioned by mental contact" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "the earth element" is a designation for non-duality; that which is called "the water element" is a designation for non-duality.
That which is called the "fire element" is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called the "wind element" is a designation made for the non-dual.
That which is called the "space element" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called the "consciousness element" is a designation for non-duality;
that which is called "ignorance" is a designation for non-duality.
That which is called "formations" is a designation made for the non-dual;
that which is called "consciousness" is a designation made for the non-dual; that which is called "name-and-form" is a designation made for the non-dual.
