for indeed, the formless attainments are not other than non-arising,
and non-arising itself is the formless attainments, while the formless attainments themselves are non-arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "formless attainments" is merely a designation for non-duality;
for indeed, the liberations are not one thing and non-arising another,
but non-arising itself is the liberations, and the liberations themselves are non-arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is called "liberations" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are not one thing and non-arising another—
non-arising itself is the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, and the successive attainments of meditative dwelling themselves are non-arising.
In this manner, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called the "attainments of the successive dwellings" is a designation for non-duality;
for indeed, the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not one thing and non-arising another.
Non-arising itself is the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are themselves non-arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is called the gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— is reckoned as non-duality; for indeed,
there is no superknowledge other than non-arising,
non-arising itself is superknowledge, and superknowledge itself is non-arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "superknowledges" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, there are no concentrations other than non-arising,
and non-arising itself is the concentrations, and the concentrations themselves are non-arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "concentrations" is a designation for non-duality;
for indeed, the gateways of dhāraṇī are not other than non-arising,
and non-arising itself is the gateways of dhāraṇī, and the gateways of dhāraṇī themselves are non-arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, those which are called "gateways to the dhāraṇīs" are designated as non-dual;
for indeed, the powers of a Tathāgata are not other than non-arising,
and non-arising itself is the powers of a Tathāgata, and the powers of a Tathāgata themselves are non-arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called the "powers of a Tathāgata" is a designation for non-duality; for indeed,
the intrepidities are not other than non-arising,
and non-arising itself is the intrepidities, and the intrepidities themselves are non-arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, those which are called "bases of self-confidence" are reckoned as non-dual;
for indeed, the analytical knowledges are not other than non-arising,
and non-arising is itself the analytical knowledges, while the analytical knowledges are themselves non-arising.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "the analytical knowledges" is a designation for non-duality;
for indeed, great loving-kindness is not other than non-arising, and non-arising itself is great loving-kindness. Great loving-kindness...

In this way, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is called "great loving-kindness" is reckoned as non-dual; for indeed, great compassion is not other than non-arising, and non-arising is not other [than great compassion].
Non-arising itself is great compassion, and great compassion itself is non-arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "great compassion" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, the unique attributes of a Buddha are not one thing and non-arising another.
Non-arising itself is the unique qualities of a Buddha; the unique qualities of a Buddha themselves are non-arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "the unique qualities of a Buddha" is reckoned as non-duality.
For indeed, the fruit of stream-entry is not other than non-arising.
Non-arising itself is the fruit of stream-entry, and the fruit of stream-entry itself is non-arising.
By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "the fruit of stream-entry" is designated as a reckoning of non-duality;
for indeed, the fruit of once-returning is not other than non-arising.
Non-arising itself is the fruit of once-returning, and the fruit of once-returning itself is non-arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called the "fruit of once-returning" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, the fruit of non-returning is not other than non-arising.
Non-arising itself is the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of non-returning itself is non-arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "the fruit of non-returning" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, Arhatship is not one thing and non-arising another.
Non-arising itself is arhatship, and arhatship itself is non-arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is called "arhatship" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, solitary awakening is not other than non-arising, and non-arising is not other [than solitary awakening].
Non-arising itself is solitary enlightenment, and solitary enlightenment itself is non-arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "solitary enlightenment" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, omniscience is not other than non-arising, and non-arising is not other than omniscience.
Non-arising itself is omniscience, and omniscience itself is non-arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called "omniscience" is designated as a reckoning of non-duality;
for indeed, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not other than non-arising.
Non-arising itself is the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of the aspects of the path itself is non-arising.
By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is called the "knowledge of the aspects of the path" is designated as non-dual;
for indeed, the knowledge of all aspects is not other than non-arising, and non-arising is not other [than it].
Non-arising itself is omniscience, and omniscience itself is non-arising.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, that which is called "omniscience" is designated as a reckoning of the non-dual.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, at the time when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, examines these phenomena in this way,
at that time, Blessed One, he perceives the non-arising of form by virtue of its absolute purity."
He perceives the non-arising of feeling by way of its ultimate purity; he perceives the non-arising of perception by way of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of mental formations by way of their ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of consciousness by virtue of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the eye by virtue of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the ear by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the nose based on its ultimate purity; one perceives the non-arising of the tongue based on its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the body based on its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the mind by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of form by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of sound by way of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of odor based on its ultimate purity; one perceives the non-arising of taste based on its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of tactile sensation based on its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of phenomena by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of eye-consciousness by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of ear-consciousness by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of olfactory consciousness by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of gustatory consciousness by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of tactile consciousness by way of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of mental consciousness by virtue of its absolute purity;
one perceives the non-arising of eye-contact by virtue of its absolute purity;
one perceives the non-arising of ear-contact by virtue of its absolute purity.
He perceives the non-arising of olfactory contact by way of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of gustatory contact by way of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of tactile contact by way of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of mental contact, by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of feeling conditioned by visual contact, by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of feeling conditioned by auditory contact, by virtue of its ultimate purity.

He perceives the non-arising of sensation conditioned by olfactory contact, on account of its ultimate purity; he perceives the non-arising of sensation conditioned by gustatory contact, on account of its ultimate purity; [he perceives the non-arising] of sensation conditioned by tactile contact... (ŚsP II-2 60)
One perceives non-arising by virtue of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of feeling conditioned by mental contact by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the earth element by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the water element by way of its ultimate purity; one perceives the non-arising of the fire element by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the wind element by way of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the space element by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the consciousness element by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of ignorance by way of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of formative forces (saṃskāra) by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of consciousness (vijñāna) by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of name-and-form (nāmarūpa) by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the six sense bases by virtue of their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of contact by virtue of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of sensation by virtue of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of craving by way of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of grasping by way of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of becoming by way of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of birth by virtue of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of old age and death by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the perfection of generosity by virtue of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the perfection of ethical discipline, by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the perfection of patience, by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the perfection of vigor, by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the perfection of meditation by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the perfection of wisdom by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of internal emptiness by way of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of external emptiness, based on its absolute purity;
he perceives the non-arising of internal-external emptiness, based on its absolute purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of emptiness, based on its absolute purity.
He perceives the non-arising of great emptiness on account of its absolute purity; he perceives the non-arising of ultimate emptiness on account of its absolute purity;
he perceives the non-arising of conditioned emptiness on account of its absolute purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of the unconditioned by virtue of its absolute purity;

one perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of the ultimate by virtue of its absolute purity; one perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end by virtue of its absolute purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of non-dispersal by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature by virtue of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics by virtue of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of the unapprehendable by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence by virtue of its ultimate purity;

one perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature by virtue of its ultimate purity; and one perceives the non-arising of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence by virtue of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the foundations of mindfulness by virtue of their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the right efforts by virtue of their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the bases of psychic power by virtue of their ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the faculties, by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the powers, by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the factors of enlightenment, by virtue of their ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the noble eightfold path by way of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the noble truths by way of their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the meditative concentrations by way of their ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the immeasurables, based on their ultimate purity; one perceives the non-arising of the formless attainments, based on their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the liberations, based on their ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings, by virtue of their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—by virtue of their ultimate purity;
and one perceives the non-arising of the superknowledges, by virtue of their ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the meditative concentrations by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the gateways of mnemonic formulas by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the powers of a Tathāgata by virtue of their ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the grounds of self-confidence by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the analytical knowledges by virtue of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of great loving-kindness by virtue of its ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of great compassion on account of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the unique qualities of a Buddha on account of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of omniscience on account of its ultimate purity.

One perceives the non-arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, by virtue of its ultimate purity; one perceives the non-arising of the knowledge of all aspects, by virtue of its ultimate purity.
(ŚsP II-2 62)
One perceives the non-arising of the ordinary person by virtue of ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the dharmas of the ordinary person by virtue of ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the stream-enterer by virtue of ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the once-returner on account of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the non-returner on account of its ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of the arhat on account of its ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the Pratyekabuddha, by virtue of its ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the dharmas of the Srotāpanna, by virtue of their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of the dharmas of the Sakṛdāgāmin, by virtue of their ultimate purity.
One perceives the non-arising of the dharmas of a non-returner based on their ultimate purity; one perceives the non-arising of the dharmas of a pratyekabuddha based on their ultimate purity;
one perceives the non-arising of a bodhisattva based on their ultimate purity.
He perceives the non-arising of the qualities of a bodhisattva on account of their ultimate purity;
he perceives the non-arising of a Buddha on account of his ultimate purity; he perceives the non-arising of the qualities of a Buddha on account of their ultimate purity.
Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the venerable Subhūti:
"As I understand the meaning of what the venerable Subhūti has spoken, form is non-arising."
The non-arising of feeling, the non-arising of perception, and the non-arising of mental formations.
Consciousness is non-arising;
the eye is non-arising,
the ear is non-arising.
The nose is non-arising; the tongue is non-arising;
the body is non-arising.
The mind is non-arising;
form is non-arising,
sound is non-arising.
Smell is non-arising;
taste is non-arising;
touch is non-arising.
All phenomena are non-arising.
Eye-consciousness is non-arising;
ear-consciousness is non-arising.
Olfactory consciousness is non-arising; gustatory consciousness is non-arising;
tactile consciousness is non-arising.
Mental consciousness is non-arising;
visual contact is non-arising,
and auditory contact is non-arising.
Olfactory contact is non-arising; gustatory contact is non-arising;
tactile contact is non-arising.
The non-arising of mental contact;
the non-arising of feeling conditioned by visual contact,
and the non-arising of feeling conditioned by auditory contact.
The non-arising of sensation conditioned by olfactory contact;
the non-arising of sensation conditioned by gustatory contact;
the non-arising of sensation conditioned by tactile contact.
The non-arising of feeling conditioned by mental contact;
the non-arising of the earth element,
the non-arising of the water element.
The fire element is non-arising;
the wind element is non-arising;
the space element is non-arising.
The element of consciousness is non-arising;
ignorance is non-arising;
the formative forces are non-arising.
Consciousness is non-arising; name-and-form is non-arising;
the six sense bases are non-arising.
Contact is non-arising; feeling is non-arising; craving is non-arising.
Grasping is non-arising;
becoming is non-arising;
birth is non-arising.
Old age and death are non-arising. The perfection of generosity is non-arising; the perfection of ethical discipline is non-arising.
the non-arising of the perfection of patience, the non-arising of the perfection of vigor,
and the non-arising of the perfection of meditative concentration;
The perfection of wisdom is non-arising.
Internal emptiness is non-arising;
external emptiness is non-arising.
The non-arising of internal-and-external emptiness, the non-arising of the emptiness of emptiness,
and the non-arising of great emptiness.
the non-arising of ultimate emptiness, the non-arising of conditioned emptiness,
and the non-arising of unconditioned emptiness;
the non-arising of absolute emptiness,
the non-arising of emptiness without beginning or end,
and the non-arising of emptiness of non-dispersal;
The non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena, and the non-arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics.
The non-arising of the emptiness of non-apprehension, the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence,
and the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is non-arising.
The applications of mindfulness are non-arising;
the right efforts are non-arising.
The bases of psychic power are non-arising; the faculties are non-arising;
the powers are non-arising.
The factors of enlightenment are non-arising; the noble eightfold path is non-arising;
the noble truths are non-arising.
The four dhyānas are non-arising;
the four immeasurables are non-arising;
the four formless attainments are non-arising.
The eight liberations are non-arising; the nine successive meditative attainments are non-arising;
the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-arising.
The superknowledges are non-arising;
the meditative concentrations are non-arising;
the gateways of mnemonic formulas are non-arising.
The ten powers of a Tathāgata are non-arising; the four fearlessnesses are non-arising;
the four analytical knowledges are non-arising.
Great loving-kindness is non-arising; great compassion is non-arising;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-arising; omniscience is non-arising.
The non-arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path,
the non-arising of the knowledge of all aspects,
and the non-arising of the ordinary person.
The dharmas of ordinary beings are non-arising;
the stream-enterer is non-arising;
the dharmas of the stream-enterer are non-arising.
The non-arising of once-returners,
the non-arising of the dharmas of once-returners,
and the non-arising of non-returners.
The dharmas of a non-returner are non-arising;
arhatship is non-arising;
the dharmas of an arhat are non-arising.
The pratyekabuddha is non-arising;
the dharmas of a pratyekabuddha are non-arising;
the bodhisattva is non-arising.
The qualities of a bodhisattva are non-arising;
the Buddha is also non-arising; the qualities of a Buddha are non-arising.
Furthermore, Venerable Subhūti, if form is non-arising,
feeling is non-arising, and perception is non-arising...
Formations are non-arising;
consciousness is non-arising.
The eye is non-arising; the ear is non-arising; the nose is non-arising; the tongue is non-arising; the body is non-arising; the mind is non-arising.
Form is non-arising; sound is non-arising; odor is non-arising; taste is non-arising; tangibles are non-arising; phenomena are non-arising.

Eye-consciousness is non-arising; ear-consciousness is non-arising; nose-consciousness is non-arising; tongue-consciousness is non-arising; body-consciousness is non-arising; mind-consciousness is non-arising.
Eye-contact is non-arising; ear-contact is non-arising; nose-contact is non-arising; tongue-contact is non-arising; body-contact is non-arising; mind-contact is non-arising.

Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by ear-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by nose-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by body-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by mind-contact is non-arising.

The earth element is non-arising; the water element is non-arising; the fire element is non-arising; the wind element is non-arising; the space element is non-arising; the consciousness element is non-arising. Ignorance is non-arising; the formative forces are non-arising; consciousness is non-arising; name-and-form is non-arising; the six sense bases are non-arising; contact is non-arising; feeling is non-arising; craving is non-arising; grasping is non-arising; becoming is non-arising.
Birth is non-arising; old age and death are non-arising.

The perfection of generosity is non-arising; the perfection of ethical discipline is non-arising; the perfection of patience is non-arising; the perfection of vigor is non-arising; the perfection of meditative concentration is non-arising; the perfection of wisdom is non-arising.
Internal emptiness is non-arising; external emptiness is non-arising; internal and external emptiness is non-arising; the emptiness of emptiness is non-arising.

The non-arising of great emptiness, the non-arising of ultimate emptiness, the non-arising of conditioned emptiness, the non-arising of unconditioned emptiness, the non-arising of absolute emptiness, the non-arising of emptiness without beginning or end, the non-arising of emptiness of non-dispersal, the non-arising of natural emptiness,
the non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena, the non-arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics, and the non-arising of the emptiness of non-apprehension.
The non-arising of the emptiness of existence, the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the non-arising of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

The non-arising of the applications of mindfulness, the non-arising of the right efforts, the non-arising of the bases of psychic power, the non-arising of the faculties, the non-arising of the powers, the non-arising of the factors of enlightenment, the non-arising of the noble eightfold path, and the non-arising of the noble truths.

Non-arising is the four dhyānas; non-arising is the four immeasurables; non-arising is the four formless attainments; non-arising is the eight liberations; non-arising is the nine successive meditative attainments;
non-arising is the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; non-arising is the superknowledges.

The concentrations are non-arising; the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are non-arising; the ten powers of a Tathāgata are non-arising; the four grounds of self-confidence are non-arising; the four analytical knowledges are non-arising; great loving-kindness is non-arising; great compassion is non-arising;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-arising; and omniscience is non-arising.
The non-arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path,
the non-arising of the knowledge of all aspects,
and the non-arising of the ordinary person.
The dharmas of ordinary persons are non-arising;
the stream-enterer is non-arising;
the dharmas of the stream-enterer are non-arising.
The non-arising of once-returners,
the non-arising of the dharmas of once-returners,
and the non-arising of non-returners.
The dharmas of a non-returner are non-arising;
arhatship is non-arising;
the dharmas of an arhat are non-arising.
The Pratyekabuddha is non-arising;
the qualities of a Pratyekabuddha are non-arising;
the Bodhisattva is non-arising.
The qualities of a bodhisattva are non-arising;

the Buddha is also non-arising, and the qualities of a Buddha are also non-arising. That which is thus attained by those following the vehicle of the śrāvakas becomes the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the attainment of arhatship itself.
By those belonging to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, pratyekabodhi is indeed attained;

by the bodhisattva mahāsattva, omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) will not be absent even amidst the distinctions of the five destinies—it is indeed attained by the bodhisattva mahāsattva as the fivefold awakening.
Venerable Subhūti, if all phenomena are non-arising, [then...]
For what reason? Because by the stream-enterer, the path has been cultivated for the abandonment of the three fetters;
by the once-returner, the path has been cultivated for the attenuation of passion, hatred, and delusion;
and by the non-returner, the path has been cultivated for the abandonment of the five lower fetters.
Has the Arhat cultivated the path for the abandonment of the five fetters that lead to rebirth in the higher realms?
Have those belonging to the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas cultivated the path for the sake of individual enlightenment?
For what reason does the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practice difficult austerities, undergoing sufferings on behalf of sentient beings?
For what reason has the Tathāgata awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
For what reason has the Tathāgata set in motion the wheel of Dharma?
When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti spoke thus to the venerable Śāradvatīputra:

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the attainment of a dharma that is unarisen, nor do I desire the state of stream-entry for one who is unarisen; I do not desire the fruit of stream-entry, nor do I desire the state of once-returning for one who is unarisen."

I do not desire the fruit of once-returning as the non-arising [of dharmas], nor do I desire the fruit of non-returning as the non-arising [of dharmas], nor do I desire the realization of arhatship as the non-arising [of dharmas].

I do not desire the state of a pratyekabuddha as the non-arising [of dharmas], nor pratyekabodhi; nor, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, do I desire that which is the bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing difficult austerities, nor even that a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives them with the notion of difficulty.
He practices. For what reason?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is not possible to accomplish the welfare of immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings after having generated the perception of suffering; rather, venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is by generating the perception of all sentient beings as one's mother that [one accomplishes their welfare].
Having formed the notion of "father" and having formed the notion of "son," it is impossible to accomplish the welfare of immeasurable and incalculable beings;
and that must be done through the yoga of non-apprehension. Thus should the mind be generated by a bodhisattva mahāsattva:
just as "self, self" is spoken of, yet that does not exist at all, in any way, or in any respect, nor is it apprehended.
In this way, one should produce a perception regarding internal and external phenomena;
if one should produce such a perception, one will produce the perception of difficulty. Why is that?
Because he does not produce any such phenomenon, nor is it apprehended; for, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in non-arising—*anutpāde*.

He asked: "But, venerable Subhūti, is there then no attainment and no realization?
Subhūti replied:
"There is, venerable Śāradvatīputra, attainment and there is realization, but not by way of the ultimate dharma."
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is by way of worldly convention that attainment or clear realization is designated;

it is by way of worldly convention that one is designated as a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, a pratyekabuddha, or a bodhisattva. But in the ultimate sense, there is neither attainment nor clear realization, nor is there a stream-enterer.
"One is designated as a once-returner, or a non-returner, or one who has attained arhatship, or a pratyekabuddha, or a bodhisattva, or a buddha.

He asked: "But, venerable Subhūti, is it just as attainment and clear realization exist through worldly convention that the distinction between the five destinies also exists through worldly convention, and not in the ultimate sense?

He replied: "It is so, venerable Śāradvatīputra; just as attainment and clear realization exist through worldly convention, so too does the distinction between the five destinies exist through worldly convention, and not [in the ultimate sense]."
Furthermore, from the perspective of ultimate reality. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in ultimate reality there is no ripening of the fruit of action;
there is neither arising nor cessation, neither affliction nor purification.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the immeasurables when they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the formless attainments when they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the liberations when they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the successive meditative absorptions when they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature."
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—once they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the superknowledges once they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the meditative concentrations once they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the gateways of dhāraṇīs that have arisen, which are empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the powers of a Tathāgata that have arisen, which are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the grounds of self-confidence that have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the analytical knowledges that have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of great loving-kindness that has arisen, for it is empty of intrinsic nature."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of great compassion when it has arisen, for it is empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the unique qualities of a Buddha when they have arisen, for they are empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the fruit of stream-entry when it has arisen, for it is empty of intrinsic nature.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the fruit of once-returning, which, having arisen, is empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the fruit of non-returning, which, having arisen, is empty of intrinsic nature;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of arhatship, which, having arisen, is empty of intrinsic nature."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the nature of self-emptiness that has arisen as individual enlightenment;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the nature of self-emptiness that has arisen as omniscience;
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the nature of self-emptiness that has arisen as the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not desire the arising of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), which, once arisen, is empty of intrinsic nature.
Śāradvatīputra asked:
"But, venerable Subhūti, does an arising arise?"
"Then does non-arising arise?
He replied: "No indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, arising does not arise, nor does non-arising arise. For what reason?"

For it is thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra: that which is arising and that which is non-arising—both these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being characterless.
Therefore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, arising does not arise.
"Non-arising does not arise.
Śāradvatīputra said:
"Venerable Subhūti, it occurs to you to speak thus: 'A non-arisen phenomenon is a non-arisen phenomenon.'"
"Venerable Subhūti, the non-arising of unarisen phenomena indeed appears to me as something to be spoken of.
Subhūti said:
"Venerable sir, 'an unarisen phenomenon, an unarisen phenomenon'..."
"Śāradvatīputra, as for what you feel inclined to say:
'An unarisen dharma is an unarisen dharma,' Venerable Śāradvatīputra, I do not feel inclined to speak of that.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, even the non-arising of unarisen dharmas does not occur to me to speak of. Why is that?"

For in this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is an unarisen dharma, that which is non-arising, that which is eloquence, those which are mantras, and that which is non-production— all these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, non-informative, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
He said: "Venerable Subhūti, 'non-arising' is the mantra; non-arising is the eloquence; non-arising is the Dharma."
"Those dharmas are also non-arisen, concerning which it is inspired eloquence to speak.
Subhūti said:
"So it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra; non-arising is the mantra, non-arising is the inspired eloquence, and non-arising is the dharma."

Those phenomena are also non-arising, concerning which it is possible to speak eloquently. Why is that? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is non-arising; feeling is non-arising; perception is non-arising; mental formations are non-arising; consciousness is non-arising.
The eye is non-arising; the ear is non-arising; the nose is non-arising; the tongue is non-arising; the body is non-arising; the mind is non-arising.
Form is non-arising; sound is non-arising; odor is non-arising; taste is non-arising; tangibility is non-arising; mental phenomena are non-arising.

Eye-consciousness is non-arising; ear-consciousness is non-arising; nose-consciousness is non-arising; tongue-consciousness is non-arising; body-consciousness is non-arising; mind-consciousness is non-arising.
Eye-contact is non-arising; ear-contact is non-arising; nose-contact is non-arising; tongue-contact is non-arising; body-contact is non-arising; mind-contact is non-arising.

Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by ear-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by nose-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by body-contact is non-arising; feeling conditioned by mind-contact is non-arising.

The earth element is non-arising; the water element is non-arising; the fire element is non-arising; the wind element is non-arising; the space element is non-arising; the consciousness element is non-arising.
Ignorance is non-arising; the formative forces are non-arising; consciousness is non-arising; name-and-form is non-arising; the six sense bases are non-arising.

Contact is non-arising; feeling is non-arising; craving is non-arising; grasping is non-arising; becoming is non-arising; birth is non-arising; old age and death are non-arising. The perfection of generosity is non-arising; the perfection of ethical discipline is non-arising; the perfection of patience is non-arising; the perfection of vigor is non-arising; the perfection of meditative concentration is non-arising; the perfection of wisdom is non-arising.

The non-arising of internal emptiness, the non-arising of external emptiness, the non-arising of internal-and-external emptiness, the non-arising of the emptiness of emptiness, the non-arising of great emptiness, the non-arising of the emptiness of the ultimate, the non-arising of the emptiness of the conditioned,

the non-arising of the emptiness of the unconditioned, the non-arising of absolute emptiness, the non-arising of the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end, the non-arising of the emptiness of non-dispersal, and the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena, the non-arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics, the non-arising of the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence, the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the non-arising of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The non-arising of the foundations of mindfulness, the non-arising of the right efforts, the non-arising of the bases of psychic power, and the non-arising of the faculties.

Non-arising is the powers; non-arising is the factors of enlightenment; non-arising is the noble eightfold path; non-arising is the noble truths; non-arising is the meditative concentrations; non-arising is the immeasurables; non-arising is the formless attainments; non-arising is the liberations; non-arising is the serial attainments.

The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-arising; the superknowledges are non-arising; the meditative concentrations are non-arising; the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are non-arising; the powers of a Tathāgata are non-arising; the grounds of self-confidence are non-arising; the analytical knowledges are non-arising; great loving-kindness is non-arising; great compassion is non-arising; and the unique qualities of a Buddha are non-arising.

The fruit of stream-entry is non-arising; the fruit of once-returning is non-arising; the fruit of non-returning is non-arising; arhatship is non-arising; pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-arising; omniscience is non-arising; knowledge of the aspects of the path is non-arising; and knowledge of all aspects is non-arising. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, non-arising is the mantra, non-arising is the eloquence, and non-arising is the Dharma.
"Even those dharmas are non-arisen, concerning which it is inspired to speak.
He said: "Venerable Subhūti should be placed at the forefront of those who discourse on the Dharma. For what reason?
Because in whatever way the Elder Subhūti is questioned, from that very point he emerges."
Subhūti said:

"This is the nature of things, venerable Śāradvatīputra, regarding the Blessed One’s disciples who are non-reliant upon all phenomena: from whatever they are questioned, from that very point they emerge. For what reason?"
This is because all phenomena are non-reliant.
He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, in what way are all phenomena non-reliant?

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, arhatship is empty by nature; it does not depend on the internal, it does not depend on the external, nor is it found between the two.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, solitary awakening is empty by nature; it does not depend on the internal, it does not depend on the external, nor is it found between the two.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is empty by nature; it does not depend on the internal, it does not depend on the external, and it is not found between the two.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is empty by nature; it does not depend on the internal, it does not depend on the external, and it is not found between the two.
Venerable [Śāradvatīputra], the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)..."
Śāradvatīputra, that [emptiness] is empty by nature; it does not depend on the internal, it does not depend on the external, nor is it found between the two.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in this manner, all phenomena are non-dependent, based upon their being empty by nature.
It is in this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having practiced the six perfections, must purify form.
Feeling is to be purified; perception is to be purified; mental formations are to be purified.
Consciousness is to be purified;
the eye is to be purified;
the ear is to be purified.
The nose is to be purified;
the tongue is to be purified;
the body is to be purified.
The mind is to be purified;
form is to be purified;
sound is to be purified.
Odor is to be purified; taste is to be purified;
touch is to be purified.
Phenomena are to be purified.
Eye-consciousness is to be purified;
ear-consciousness is to be purified.
Olfactory consciousness is to be purified; gustatory consciousness is to be purified;
tactile consciousness is to be purified.
Mental consciousness is to be purified;
eye-contact is to be purified;
ear-contact is to be purified.
The contact of the nose is to be purified;
the contact of the tongue is to be purified;
the contact of the body is to be purified.
Mental contact is to be purified.
Feeling conditioned by visual contact is to be purified;
feeling conditioned by auditory contact is to be purified.
The sensation conditioned by olfactory contact is to be purified;
the sensation conditioned by gustatory contact is to be purified;
the sensation conditioned by tactile contact is to be purified.
Feeling conditioned by mental contact is to be purified.
The earth element is to be purified; the water element is to be purified; the fire element is to be purified; the wind element is to be purified; the space element is to be purified;
and the consciousness element is to be purified.
Ignorance is to be purified;
volitional formations are to be purified;
consciousness is to be purified.
Name-and-form is to be purified; the six sense bases are to be purified;
contact is to be purified; feeling is to be purified.
Craving is to be purified;
grasping is to be purified;
becoming is to be purified; birth is to be purified.
Old age and death are to be purified;
the perfection of generosity is to be purified,
and the perfection of ethical discipline is to be purified.
The perfection of patience is to be purified;
the perfection of vigor is to be purified;
the perfection of meditation is to be purified.
The perfection of wisdom is to be purified;
internal emptiness is to be purified;
external emptiness is to be purified.
Internal-external emptiness is to be purified;
the emptiness of emptiness is to be purified;
great emptiness is to be purified.
Ultimate emptiness is to be purified;
conditioned emptiness is to be purified;
unconditioned emptiness is to be purified.
The emptiness of the ultimate should be purified; the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end should be purified;
the emptiness of non-dispersal should be purified.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature must be purified;
the emptiness of all phenomena must be purified;
the emptiness of specific characteristics must be purified.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is to be purified; the emptiness of non-existence is to be purified;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is to be purified.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is to be purified;
the applications of mindfulness are to be purified;
the right efforts are to be purified.
The bases of psychic power are to be purified; the faculties are to be purified;
the powers are to be purified.
The factors of enlightenment are to be purified;
the noble eightfold path is to be purified;
the noble truths are to be purified.
The meditative absorptions are to be purified;
the immeasurables are to be purified;
the formless attainments are to be purified.
The liberations are to be purified;
the nine successive meditative attainments are to be purified; and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are to be purified.
The superknowledges are to be purified; the meditative concentrations are to be purified;
the gateways of mnemonic formulas are to be purified.
The powers of a Tathāgata are to be purified; the grounds of self-confidence are to be purified; the analytical knowledges are to be purified.
Great loving-kindness is to be purified; great compassion is to be purified;
the unique qualities of a Buddha are to be purified.
Omniscience is to be purified; the knowledge of the aspects of the path is to be purified;
the knowledge of all aspects is to be purified.
Then, venerable Śāradvatīputra, spoke again to the venerable Subhūti:
"Venerable Subhūti, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the six perfections, purify the path to awakening?
Subhūti replied:
In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is a mundane perfection of generosity and there is a supramundane [perfection of generosity];
there is a mundane perfection of ethical discipline and there is a supramundane [perfection of ethical discipline].
The perfection of patience is both mundane and supramundane;
the perfection of vigor is both mundane and supramundane;
the perfection of meditation is both mundane and supramundane.
The perfection of wisdom is both mundane and supramundane.
He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what is the mundane perfection of giving, and what is the supramundane?
Subhūti replied:
In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva becomes a giver and a lord of giving toward śramaṇas, brahmins, the wretched, beggars, mendicants, and supplicants:

food to those seeking food, drink to those seeking drink, vehicles to those seeking vehicles, clothing to those seeking clothing, flowers to those seeking flowers, garlands to those seeking garlands, perfumes to those seeking perfumes, and ointments.

To those who desired ointments, he gave ointments; to those who desired a dwelling, he gave a dwelling; to those who desired bedding and seats, he gave bedding and seats; to those who desired requisites, he gave requisites; to those who desired medicine, he gave medicine; and so on, up to giving various human necessities to those who desired them. To those who desired sons, he gave sons; to those who desired daughters, he gave daughters; and to those who desired wives, he gave wives.
He gives kingdoms to those who seek kingdoms;
he gives his head to those who seek his head; he gives his eyes to those who seek his eyes.
He gives his limbs to those who require limbs;
he gives his flesh, blood, and marrow to those who require flesh, blood, and marrow; and while giving these, he does so with a basis, thinking thus:
"I give; he receives; this is the gift; I am the giver;
I am the lord of giving; I am the renouncer of all possessions."
"I am carrying out the command of the Buddha; I am practicing the perfection of generosity;
and having given that gift, by way of apprehension, I shall share it in common with all sentient beings for the sake of unsurpassed [enlightenment]."
He dedicates it toward perfect enlightenment, thinking, "By this fruit of my giving, may these beings be happy in this very life and attain final nirvāṇa without clinging";
yet, he gives that gift while being attached to the three types of conjunctions.

In which three? Namely, being attached to these three associations—namely, the notion of self, the notion of another, and the notion of giving—one gives a gift. This is called the mundane perfection of generosity (*laukikī dānapāramitā*). For what reason is it called the mundane perfection of generosity?
For it does not proceed from the world, nor does it emerge from it, nor does it transmigrate; therefore it is called the mundane perfection of generosity.
In that regard, what is the supramundane perfection of generosity?
That is to say, the purity of the three spheres.
In that regard, what is the purity of the three spheres?

Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva gives that gift, he does not apprehend a self, he does not apprehend a recipient, he does not apprehend the gift, nor does he [apprehend] the maturation.
And he does not take delight in it. This, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s purity of the three spheres.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, he gives a gift to all sentient beings and dedicates that gift to them, yet he does not apprehend those sentient beings;
he dedicates it to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and yet he does not perceive any sign. This, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is called the supramundane perfection of giving. By what...
For what reason is it called the supramundane perfection of giving?
Because it moves through and transcends the world, it is therefore called the supramundane perfection of giving.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is a mundane perfection of ethical discipline, and there is a supramundane one.

In that regard, what is the mundane perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*)? Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva guards ethical discipline, yet he does so with a basis; it occurs to him: "I guard ethical discipline for the sake of sentient beings. This ethical discipline is the command of the Buddha."

While guarding that morality, he performs it by way of apprehension; having made it common to all sentient beings, he dedicates it to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, thinking: "By this fruit of my morality, may these sentient beings be happy in this very life and attain parinirvāṇa without further clinging. Thus, being attached to the three perceptions, he guards that morality.
That is to say: the notion of self, the notion of others, and the notion of ethical discipline—this is called the mundane perfection of ethical discipline (*laukikī śīlapāramitā*).
For it does not proceed from the world, it does not transcend it, and it does not pass beyond it; therefore, it is called "mundane.
In that regard, what is the supramundane perfection of ethical discipline (*lokottarā śīlapāramitā*)?
Namely, the purity of the three spheres.
In that regard, what is the purity of the three spheres?
Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while guarding ethical discipline, does not perceive a self.

One does not perceive sentient beings; one does not perceive the precepts; one does not delight in their maturation; and one dedicates those precepts to all sentient beings. Yet, one does not perceive those sentient beings [as real entities] while dedicating them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, nor does one perceive any sign. This is called the supramundane perfection of ethical discipline (*lokottara-śīlapāramitā*). It is thus.
For it moves through the world, rises above the world, and transcends the world; therefore, it is called "supramundane.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is a mundane perfection of patience and there is a supramundane one.
In that regard, what is the mundane perfection of patience?
In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates patience and becomes dependent upon it; he thinks to himself: "I cultivate patience for the sake of all sentient beings."

"This patience performs the command of the Buddha. While cultivating that patience by way of apprehension (*upalambha*), he makes it common with all sentient beings and dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, [thinking]:
"By this fruit of my patience, may these sentient beings be happy in this very life and attain parinirvāṇa without further grasping (*anupādāya*)."

Thus, being attached to these three perceptions, he cultivates those forms of patience—namely, the perception of self, the perception of others, and the perception of patience. This is called the mundane perfection of patience (*laukikī kṣāntipāramitā*). For it does not course, does not transcend, and does not transition beyond the world; therefore, it is called "mundane."
In that regard, what is the supramundane perfection of patience?
It is the complete purity of the three spheres.
In that regard, what is the complete purity of the three spheres?

In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while cultivating patience, does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend sentient beings, and does not apprehend patience; he does not delight in its maturation,
and he dedicates that patience to all sentient beings, yet he does not apprehend those sentient beings.
One dedicates [this] toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, yet one does not perceive any sign. This is called the supramundane perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*);
for it moves away from, rises above, and transcends the world, and thus it is called "supramundane.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is a mundane perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*) and there is a supramundane one.
In that regard, what is the mundane perfection of vigor?
Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts vigor, and he exerts it while being dependent [on something]. It occurs to him: "I exert vigor for the sake of all sentient beings."
"This is the body, this is the mind, this is the vigor; I am carrying out the command of the Buddha, I am practicing the perfection of vigor.
And having made that vigor common to all sentient beings through the application of apprehension (*upalambha-yoga*), he dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, thinking:
"By this fruit of my vigor, may these sentient beings be happy in this very life and attain final nirvana without further clinging. Thus, being attached to these three notions, he exerts that vigor.

That is to say: the perception of self, the perception of others, and the perception of vigor—this is called the mundane perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*). For it does not course, does not proceed, and does not transition from the perspective of the world; therefore, it is called "mundane. In that regard, what is the supramundane perfection of vigor?
That is to say, the purity of the three spheres.
In that regard, what is the purity of the three spheres?
Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while exerting vigor, does not apprehend a self.

One does not apprehend sentient beings, one does not apprehend vigor, and one does not delight in its maturation; one dedicates that vigor for the sake of all sentient beings, yet one does not apprehend those sentient beings; and even while dedicating it toward unexcelled perfect enlightenment, one does not perceive any sign—this is called the supramundane perfection of vigor, for thus it is.
It moves away from the world, rises above it, and transcends it; therefore, it is called "supramundane.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is a mundane perfection of meditation and there is a supramundane one.
In that regard, what is the mundane perfection of meditation?

In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva enters into meditative absorption, yet he enters it while remaining dependent [upon a basis]. It occurs to him: "For the sake of all sentient beings, I enter into these meditative absorptions;
these are the meditative absorptions."

"I carry out the command of the Buddha, and while entering that meditative absorption, having made it common to all sentient beings through the application of non-apprehension, he dedicates it toward unexcelled perfect enlightenment, thinking: 'By this fruit of my meditation, may these sentient beings become happy in this very life and attain final nirvana without clinging.'"

Attached to three notions, he enters that meditative absorption— namely, the notion of self, the notion of another, and the notion of meditative absorption; this is called the mundane perfection of meditation,
for it does not proceed from the world, does not transcend it, and does not pass beyond it.
That is called "worldly.
In that regard, what is the supramundane perfection of meditative concentration?
It is, namely, the complete purity of the three spheres.
In that regard, what is the purity of the three spheres?

Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while entering the meditative absorptions, does not perceive a self, does not perceive sentient beings, and does not take delight in the maturation [of the results];
and he dedicates those meditative absorptions for the sake of all sentient beings.
And those beings are not apprehended;

yet he dedicates [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and moreover, he does not perceive any sign. This is called the supramundane perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*), for it moves away from, rises above, and transcends the world;
therefore, it is called "supramundane."
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is a mundane perfection of wisdom and there is a supramundane perfection of wisdom.
In that regard, what is the mundane perfection of wisdom?
Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates wisdom."
Relying upon that, he cultivates it; he confesses all evil;

for the sake of himself and others, he rejoices in all merit and entreats all the Buddhas by way of apprehension (*upalambha-yogena*); and he dedicates all those roots of virtue toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of non-expedient means (*anupāya*). For him who acts thus:
He thinks, "I am cultivating wisdom for the sake of all sentient beings; this is wisdom; I am carrying out this command of the Buddha.

And while cultivating that wisdom, by means of the yoga of apprehension, he makes it common to all sentient beings and dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, thinking: "By this fruit of my wisdom, may these sentient beings [be seen]..."
Thinking, "May they be happy in this very Dharma and enter parinirvāṇa without further rebirth," he cultivates that wisdom while being attached to three perceptions—
namely, the perception of self, the perception of others, and the perception of wisdom. This is called mundane [wisdom].
The perfection of wisdom does not move through the worlds, does not transcend them, and does not pass beyond them; therefore it is called "worldly.
In that regard, what is the supramundane perfection of wisdom?
It is the complete purity of the three spheres.
In that regard, what is the purity of the three spheres?

Here, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while cultivating wisdom, does not perceive a self, does not perceive sentient beings, and does not perceive wisdom; yet he dedicates that wisdom for the sake of all sentient beings.
And since those beings are not apprehended, one dedicates [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment while yet not perceiving any sign;
this is called supramundane perfection of wisdom. For it moves away from, rises above, and transcends the world; therefore it is called the supramundane perfection of wisdom.
"In this way indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the six perfections purifies the path to awakening.
He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
Subhūti replied:
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of generosity is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of ethical discipline is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of patience is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The perfection of vigor is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of meditative concentration is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the perfection of wisdom is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, internal emptiness is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
external emptiness is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and internal-external emptiness is the path to awakening for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The emptiness of emptiness is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the great emptiness is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of the ultimate truth is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The emptiness of the conditioned is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of the unconditioned is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the absolute emptiness is the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of non-dispersal is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The emptiness of all phenomena is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of specific characteristics is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of non-existence is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The four foundations of mindfulness, venerable Śāradvatīputra, are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the four right endeavors are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The four bases of miraculous power are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the five faculties are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the five powers are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The seven factors of enlightenment are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the noble eightfold path is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the four noble truths are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The four dhyānas are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the four immeasurables are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the four formless attainments are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

The eight liberations are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The five superknowledges are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
all meditative concentrations are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and all doors of dhāraṇīs are the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the ten powers of a Tathāgata are the path to enlightenment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the four grounds of self-confidence are the path to enlightenment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
the four analytical knowledges are the path to enlightenment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Great loving-kindness is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; great compassion is the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are the path to awakening for the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
He said: "Excellent, excellent, venerable Subhūti! Of which perfection is this the heroic power?
Subhūti replied:
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this is the heroic power of the perfection of wisdom. For what reason?"

For in this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of wisdom is the mother of all wholesome dharmas— of the dharmas of the śrāvakas, the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, and the dharmas of the buddhas;
the perfection of wisdom, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is the sustainer and the gatherer of all wholesome dharmas.

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by practicing the perfection of wisdom— the dharma of the śrāvakas, the dharma of the bodhisattvas, and the dharma of the buddhas— past Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones will likewise [awaken] in this very perfection of wisdom."

Having practiced it, he will awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas who currently reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the world systems in the ten directions—
they too, having practiced right here in this perfection of wisdom, have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, if when the perfection of wisdom is being taught, there is neither hesitation nor despondency in a bodhisattva mahāsattva, it should be known, Venerable Śāradvatīputra,
that this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this dwelling, namely, for the protection of all sentient beings.
For the sake of not abandoning all sentient beings, that bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells by way of non-apprehension through this mental engagement, namely, the mental engagement of great compassion.
He said: "Venerable Subhūti, you wish for this bodhisattva mahāsattva to dwell by means of this dwelling?"
And if one is not separated from this mental attention—that is, the mental attention of great compassion—then, Venerable Subhūti, all sentient beings would become bodhisattvas. Why is that?
Because, Venerable Subhūti, all sentient beings are indeed never separated from mental attention.

Subhūti said: "Excellent, excellent, venerable Śāradvatīputra! 'I shall reprove, I shall reprove'—it is for this very reason that you, venerable Śāradvatīputra, have been accepted by means of your speaking of words that accord with reality. Why is that?

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the non-existence of sentient beings, the non-existence of mental attention should be understood; through the absence of sentient beings, the absence of mental attention should be understood; through the lack of intrinsic nature of sentient beings, the lack of intrinsic nature of mental attention should be understood."
Through the emptiness of sentient beings, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood;

through the seclusion of sentient beings, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood; through the non-awakening of sentient beings, the non-awakening of mental attention should be understood.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by the non-existence of form, the non-existence of mental attention should be known;
by the absence of form, the absence of mental attention should be known; by the lack of intrinsic nature in form, the lack of intrinsic nature in mental attention should be known.
It should be understood that through the emptiness of form, the emptiness of mental attention is to be understood;
through the seclusion of form, the seclusion of mental attention is to be understood;
and through the non-realization of form, the non-realization of mental attention is to be understood.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by the non-existence of feeling, the non-existence of mental attention should be known;

by the absence of being of feeling, the absence of being of mental attention should be known; by the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling, the lack of intrinsic nature of mental attention should be known.
Through the emptiness of feeling, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood;
through the seclusion of feeling, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood;
through the non-awakening to feeling, the non-awakening to mental attention should be understood.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by the non-existence of perception, the non-existence of mental attention should be known;
by the absence of perception, the absence of mental attention should be known;
by the lack of intrinsic nature in perception, the lack of intrinsic nature in mental attention should be known.

Through the emptiness of perception, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood; through the seclusion of perception, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood; through the non-realization of perception, the non-realization of mental attention should be understood.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, the non-existence of mental attention should be known;

by the absence of conditioned phenomena, the absence of mental attention should be known; by the lack of intrinsic nature in conditioned phenomena, the lack of intrinsic nature in mental attention should be known.

Through the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood; through the seclusion of conditioned phenomena, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood; through the non-realization of conditioned phenomena, the non-realization of mental attention should be understood.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by the non-existence of consciousness, the non-existence of mental attention should be understood;
by the absence of consciousness, the absence of mental attention should be understood;
by the lack of intrinsic nature in consciousness, the lack of intrinsic nature in mental attention should be understood.

Through the emptiness of consciousness, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood; through the seclusion of consciousness, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood; through the non-awakening to consciousness, the non-awakening to mental attention should be understood.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by the non-existence of the eye, the non-existence of mental attention should be known;
by the absence of the eye, the absence of mental attention should be known;
by the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye, the lack of intrinsic nature of mental attention should be known.
Through the emptiness of the eye, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood;
through the seclusion of the eye, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood;
through the non-awakening to the eye, the non-awakening to mental attention should be understood.

Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the venerable Subhūti:
Excellent, excellent, Subhūti!

It is indeed in this way, Subhūti, that the perfection of wisdom should be taught to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, just as you have taught it—and that too through the power of the Tathāgata. Furthermore, it is in this manner that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

It is exactly as you teach. Furthermore, while this discourse on the perfection of wisdom was being spoken by the venerable Subhūti, this great trichiliocosm shook in six ways: it quaked, it quaked violently, it quaked intensely; it trembled, it trembled violently, it trembled intensely.
It moved, it moved forward, it moved completely forward;
it was agitated,
it was agitated forward, it was agitated completely forward.
It roared, it roared forth, it roared completely; it resounded, it resounded forth, it resounded completely;
the eastern direction sank down.
The western direction rose up,
the eastern direction rose up,
and the western direction sank down.
The northern direction sank down,
the southern direction rose up;
the northern direction rose up.
The southern direction sank down;
it sank down in the middle and rose up at the edges.
It sank down at the edges and rose up in the middle.
Then, at that moment, the Blessed One manifested a smile.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for manifesting a smile?
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:

Subhūti, just as I here in this Sahā world-system teach this perfection of wisdom, even so in the countless and immeasurable world-systems in the eastern direction, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas teach this very perfection of wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

all the Bṛhatphala devaputras in the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system, together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devaputras, [also] assembled there in that very assembly.

All the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host within the triple-thousand great-thousand world-system, together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of other sons of the gods, assembled right there in that assembly; and as for the bodily radiance produced by the ripening of karma belonging to those gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika host within the triple-thousand great-thousand world-system—

Whatever bodily radiance those gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three possess, born of the maturation of their karma; whatever bodily radiance those Yāma gods possess, born of the maturation of their karma; and whatever bodily radiance those Tuṣita gods possess, born of the maturation of their karma—
Whatever bodily radiance those gods of the Nirmāṇarati heaven possess, born of the maturation of their karma;

whatever bodily radiance those gods of the Paranirmitavaśavartin heaven possess, born of the maturation of their karma; and whatever bodily radiance those gods of the Brahmakāyika heaven possess, born of the maturation of their karma—
And whatever bodily radiance those Ābhāsvara gods possess, born of the maturation of karma, and whatever bodily radiance those Śubhakṛtsna gods possess, born of the maturation of karma—
The bodily radiance of those Bṛhatphala gods, which arises from the ripening of karma, and the bodily radiance of those Śuddhāvāsakāyika gods, which arises from the ripening of karma—
neither approaches even a hundredth part of the Tathāgata’s natural radiance.
It does not approach even a thousandth part, it does not approach even a hundred-thousandth part,
nor does it approach even a hundred-thousand-koṭī-niyuta-th part.
It does not admit of comparison even by number, fraction, calculation, analogy, or resemblance.
In the presence of the Tathāgata’s natural radiance, all those radiances of the gods born of the maturation of karma do not shine, do not glow, and do not gleam.

This radiance of the Tathāgata is called supreme, it is called the eldest, it is called distinguished, it is called excellent, it is called pre-eminent, it is called sublime, it is called unsurpassed, and it is called peerless.

How, Venerable Subhūti, should a bodhisattva mahāsattva stand in the perfection of wisdom?
"And what is the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? And how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom?
When this was said, the venerable Subhūti spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:

Therefore, Kauśika, listen well and attend closely; I shall teach by the power of the Buddha and through the Buddha’s empowerment how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should abide in the perfection of wisdom and how they should train therein. And for those sons of the gods who have [set out] for unexcelled...

Those who have not yet generated the mind set on perfect enlightenment should also generate the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. However, those who have already entered the fixed course of rightness are no longer capable of generating the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Why is that?
For you have established a boundary against the stream of saṃsāra.
Nevertheless, I indeed rejoice even in them, provided they generate the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

"I do not create an obstacle for their side of wholesome qualities; rather, one should take as one's objective those most excellent dharmas that are more distinguished than already distinguished dharmas.
In this regard, Kauśika, what is the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
Here, Kauśika, by means of the production of a thought associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), a bodhisattva mahāsattva..."
